rootCause.what: the closure's mainProof verdict requires `merge.parentCount === 1`, because the loop's merge method is a squash merge. The pin fabricated the merge commit as the AMBIENT checkout's HEAD (`headSha = git(['rev-parse','HEAD'], repoRoot)` in beforeAll) and had the fake gh report it. On a `pull_request` event actions/checkout@v6 leaves HEAD at refs/pull/N/merge, which is a TWO-parent commit, so the closure computed parentCount 2, wrote verdict FAIL and refused with MAIN_PROOF_NOT_PASS - correctly, on the input the pin gave it.
rootCause.notAPlatformDefect: the charter framed this as "passes on Windows, fails on Linux". It is not an OS difference: the variable is the checkout ref. Measured both ways - the same fixture exits 0 on Linux when the fabricated merge commit has one parent, and exits 1 on Windows when it has two.
rootCause.whyItPassedLocally: `git rev-list --parents -n 1 HEAD` in this worktree prints `fb2adc7e1e3dabcb4168285e0aa1642b8370a044 f018e34cc150d9ede58e39a32929c5c9dec7d9b6` - one parent, because the worktree is detached on the PR head itself rather than on the merge ref.

candidatesRuledOut.candidate: (a) the fake gh the pin writes on PATH is a Windows-only shape (a .cmd file, or a file without the executable bit, or a shebang-less script), so spawnSync('gh') fails on POSIX
candidatesRuledOut.evidence: the pin already branches on process.platform and writes a `#!/bin/sh` shim at mode 0o755 on POSIX (lines 355-362 of the staged file). The Linux arm of E7 exercised exactly that branch and exited 0, which requires three successful gh calls (pr view, pr view --json files, pr checks). Independently in CI: the case 'refuses a review that does not name the reviewer model' asserts `result.stderr` contains 'reviewerModel', and it PASSED on ubuntu - that refusal is downstream of both `gh pr view` calls, so gh resolved and parsed there too.

candidatesRuledOut.candidate: (b) the fake gh or the closure resolves gh through gh.cmd/PATHEXT logic that only exists on win32
candidatesRuledOut.evidence: the closure's gh helper spawns `gh <args>` with `shell: true`, which resolves a mode-0755 shim through /bin/sh on POSIX and the .cmd shim through cmd.exe on Windows. Both were measured green in E7, and CI's own passing refusal cases prove the POSIX resolution worked on ubuntu.

candidatesRuledOut.candidate: (c) the U13 preserveRunLogs call refuses on POSIX for a path-expressibility reason (the proof directory or preserved root under os.tmpdir() relative to the temporary ledger's repo root)
candidatesRuledOut.evidence: in CI itself the case 'preserves the proof logs even when the verdict is FAIL' PASSED: it reads evidence/u91-logs-20260917.json out of the temporary ledger and compares its file list against fs.readdirSync(proofDir). The manifest therefore existed and listed the right ten files on ubuntu. Both Linux arms of E7 also reported `logs manifest: true`.

candidatesRuledOut.candidate: (d) a \r\n / \n or path-separator assumption in the receipt comparison
candidatesRuledOut.evidence: the Linux one-parent arm of E7 ran the identical fixture end to end to exit 0, verdict PASS, unit complete - every log line parsed, every receipt written and read. In CI the FAIL-path cases read the mainProof receipt and the logs manifest successfully. No comparison in the file is sensitive to the separator.

fix.productModulesUnchanged: scripts/qc/roadmap-unit-closure.mjs sha256 7b3ba7aa08be8bfff87607a4312324fb266c8dca924f41683c68d50f7c1f2e9d and scripts/qc/roadmap-main-proof.mjs sha256 82fd00ecd12e1fc202768d504ef777f20f5192db25c52129fb499aa04f591227 are byte-identical to revision 1. The closure's one-parent requirement is correct behaviour for a squash merge and was not weakened; the pin was fabricating an input the closure is right to refuse.
changes: beforeAll builds a throwaway git repository under os.tmpdir() with three commits, so HEAD and HEAD~1 each have exactly one parent; headSha and earlierSha come from it and closureArgs carries `--repo-root <that repository>`. No case reads the checkout's own HEAD any more, so no checkout ref can change a verdict.

expectClosureOk(result) replaces the six bare `expect(result.status).toBe(0)` assertions: same condition, but it throws with the closure's stderr AND stdout, so the next CI failure names its refusal instead of printing 1.
the 'refuses when the checkout is not at the merge commit' case strips --repo-root from closureArgs before naming its own, rather than relying on last-flag-wins.
two small dedups the change would otherwise duplicate: `without(args, flag)` generalises `withoutLedgerDir`, and PIN_GIT_ENV + commitAll() replace three copies of the commit-identity block.
